paragraphs: Originally formed in the early 1970's as the 'Ice Hockey Club', the team was co-ed and went through several names including 'Wolfpuck' while playing out of Greensboro.

At the time, the roster was primarily made up of out-of-state or Canadian students looking for a slice of home while pursuing degrees in forestry. Hockey had yet to gain widespread popularity outside of northern regions.
The first official game was played in the Fall of 1976, establishing the foundation for fifty seasons of collegiate ice hockey at NC State University.

paragraphs: In 1995, NC State joined the newly formed Atlantic Coast Conference Hockey League (ACCHL), becoming one of the league's Original Eight founding members. The team went 7–7–0 in the inaugural season.
In 1997, the Carolina Hurricanes franchise relocated to North Carolina, igniting a hockey boom across the Triangle and inspiring new generations of student-athletes to lace up their skates.

In 2001, the team tasted victory for the first time as ACCHL Season Champions. This Wolfpuck team achieved the first three-peat in program history, claiming Season Championships in 2001, 2002, and 2003 before lifting the Admiral's Cup as League Champions in 2003.

Hall of Famer Nick Sabo (1999–2004: Team Captain, Tournament MVP, ACCHL 1st-Team All-Star D) alongside All-ACCHL standouts Josh Cottrell (1st team F), Jorge Alves (1st team G), Brandon Gregor (2nd team F), Travis Sharpstene (2nd team D), and Josh Matteo under head coach Mike Young cemented the Wolfpuck legacy of earning semi-final appearances through fearless, physical play.
Throughout the mid-2000s, the Wolfpack continued competing across the Mid-Atlantic, building out institutional support and fan traditions across the Triangle.

On July 4, 2009, the program suffered the tragic loss of beloved goaltender Stephen Russell. In his honor, the program established the annual Stephen Russell Memorial Tournament, which continues today as one of the premier collegiate invitational tournaments on the East Coast.

In 2010, Mike Gazzillo assumed the head coach position. Over a storied ten-year tenure, the future ACCHL Hall of Fame coach guided the program to unprecedented national prominence with celebrated players including Harry Fryckberg, Nick Christopoulos, Tyler Cloutier, Sam Banasiewicz, Luis Giminez, Riley Johnson, Chris Solomon, Parker Szarek, and Garrett Auriene.
The Icepack captured ACCHL Season Championships six times during this decade (2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2019, and 2020), and hoisted the Admiral's Cup as League Champions in 2011, 2019, and 2020.
At the conclusion of the 2019–20 championship campaign, longtime assistant Tim Healy was promoted to Head Coach to lead the next chapter of the program.

The Icepack safely competed and captured the Admiral's Cup during the 2021 pandemic season, proving the program's resilience under adversity. Former Head Coach Mike Gazzillo was inducted into the Class of 2021 ACCHL Hall of Fame.

As part of the 2023 NHL Stadium Series festivities, the NC State Icepack faced archrival UNC Chapel Hill at Carter-Finley Stadium for the historic 'Frozen Finley Outdoor Game' in front of a record-setting crowd of 24,000+ fans. The Icepack routed the Tar Heels 7–3 — a touchdown to a field goal as an homage to the football stadium.

In May 2024, the Icepack was formally approved as inaugural members of the new ACCHL Men's Division I Conference expansion. In 2025, the Stephen Russell Tournament returned home to Raleigh for the first time in seven years.

Signaling the end of an era, Tim Healy stepped down as head coach following the inaugural Division I campaign. The team finished 8–2–0 in conference and 20–12–1 overall (3rd in MD1 ACCHL and 38th overall nationally in ACHA).
image_caption: Carter-Finley Stadium during the 2023 Frozen Finley Outdoor Game (24,000+ fans)

paragraphs: On July 1, 2026, Nagib Ward took over as Head Coach to lead the 50th Anniversary Golden Season.
On September 11, 2026, the 50th Season kicked off at Lane Arena with a 4–2 victory over Virginia Tech.

Now competing in the SECHL (Southeastern Collegiate Hockey League) at the ACHA Division I level, the Icepack continues its pursuit of a Top 24 national computer ranking to earn a bid to the ACHA National Tournament in St. Louis, Missouri.
